figures.title: Figure 1
figures.llm_description: FIG. 1. Polar material properties of interest differentiate by the degree of polar ordering, including paraelectrics, relaxors/dipolar glasses, antiferroelectrics, and ferroelectrics.

figures.title: Figure 2
figures.llm_description: FIG. 2. The structure of the (a) in-layer and (b) in-gap FE phase in CIPS. The position of Cu atoms is indicated schematically through a distribution function. The orientation of the polarization for the specific Cu position is indicated in black arrows. (c) DFT calculations of the in-layer and in-gap FE phases as a function of c-lattice parameter. Adapted with permission from Brehm et al., Nat. Mater. 19, 43 (2020).

figures.title: Figure 3
figures.llm_description: FIG. 3. The structure of three different AFE phases in CIPS for (a) interlayer and (b) and (c) intralayer AFE ordering. (d) Energy of the three AFE phases with respect to the FE phase. Adapted with permission from Neumayer et al., ACS Nano 16, 2452 (2022).

figures.title: Figure 4
figures.llm_description: FIG. 4. Mechanisms for transitions between dissimilar FE phases in CIPS. (a) Temperature dependent phase transitions: Piezoresponse images (top) and diagram (bottom) as a function of temperature. The LP phases convert to �HP before the non-polar phase is reached above the Curie temperature.
